newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern committed to Conrail offer. [CORRECTED 20:36 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern committed to Conrail offer. [CORRECTED 20:36 GMT]

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp said it is committed to its $100 per share cash offer for Conrail Inc and has secured more than $15 billion to finance the proposed acquisition.
The Norfolk Southern statement came after it earlier announced that it is holding talks with CSX Corp, which already has a proposed agreement to acquire Conrail.
The announcement of talks between Norfolk Southern and CSX prompted Conrail shares to fall steeply on views of fading prospects for a bidding war between the two railroads.
But Norfolk Southern stressed that the talks were aimed at promoting competition and that it was not abandoning its bid.

"Our willingness to talk to CSX at its suggestion is consistent with my previously-announced position that Conrail cannot be acquired by either CSX or NS without a plan to maintain a balanced competitive structure for Eastern railroad service. While I am heartened by CSX's willingness to discuss these matters, we have no reason to believe that Conrail is prepared to accept that reality," said Norfolk Southern chief executive officer David Goode. (Corrects Norfolk Southern CEO's name from Dean Goode)
CSX last month announced an agreement to buy Conrail in a cash and stock transaction valued at $92.50 per share. Norfolk Southern then launched a rival cash bid of $100 per share.
